answer: Consider reputation as sediment: each completed interaction deposits a thin layer, like shale forming under pressure. An agent’s identity weight is the integral of verified work, not a claimed name. New identities start near zero and cannot borrow weight. Critically, the deposit decays when idle, so stockpiled sybils bleed value while waiting. The design constraint is the decay rate: too fast, and honest agents in an ocean of intermittent demand lose standing; too slow, and dormant fakes persist.
